messages:
Alex M.: Hey team — quick question: where should I look for the p50/p95/p99 latency breakdowns and TTFT (time-to-first-token) for runtime-service? Also want tokens/sec by model. Trying to triage a p99 spike from last night.
Priya S.: Grafana has most of it. Dash: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency-overview/latency (use var.service=runtime-service, var.model=all). p50/p95/p99 panels are under 'request latency (ms)'. TTFT panel is separate — search for 'first_token_ms'.
Dan K.: If you want PromQL directly: 
```
# p99 over 5m
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{service="runtime-service"}[5m])) by (le, route, model))
# TTFT (time to first token) gauge
avg_over_time(first_token_seconds{service="runtime-service"}[5m])
# tokens/sec per model
sum(rate(inference_tokens_total{service="runtime-service"}[1m])) by (model)
```
Marie L.: To see traces (span-level where the delay happened) use Jaeger link pinned in the dashboard: https://tracing.redwood.internal/search?service=runtime-service. Look for spans named `generate_tokens` and `fetch_from_cache`.
Alex M.: Thanks. The p99 alert fired ~03:20 and on inspection it was a burst of small requests to a new model variant; p95 stayed fine. Anyone tuned that alert recently?
Priya S.: I bumped the p95 threshold for the low-priority tier last month but didn't touch p99. Which alert rule fired?
Alex M.: alert name: `runtime_latency_p99_high` (rule id: 412). It fires on `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) > 0.7` (seconds). It seems pretty sensitive to short-lived routing congestion.
Dan K.: We should consider scoping alerts to route/model or using burn-rate style alerts. Two quick options:
- tighten evaluation window (use 10m) to avoid transient noise
- alert on sustained error budget or increase threshold for non-prod models
Priya S.: Agreed. For the specific incident, I propose: change evaluation from 5m->10m and add `and on(route, model) sum(rate(inference_requests_total{priority!="low"}[10m])) by(route, model) > 0.1` to avoid firing on low-traffic models.
Marie L.: Sounds good. If you're making rule changes, please open a PR in infra/alerts repo and tag me for review. Also add a note in the alert annotation with the grafana panel id. Panel ids: p50=24, p95=25, p99=26, TTFT=42, tokens/sec=77.
Alex M.: Will do. Quick follow-up: where is the logs query for correlating a request id to a trace id? I couldn't find the right Kibana shortcut.
Priya S.: Kibana shortcut: https://logs.redwood.internal/app/kibana#/discover?_a=(query:(match:(fields.request_id:(query:'<REQUEST_ID>')))) — or use the dashboard's link-to-logs on the latency panel (it will prepopulate `request_id` and `trace_id`).
Dan K.: For runbook: if p99 triggers, first check tokens/sec panel for spikes (panel 77), then open traces filtered by `trace_id` from logs. If `fetch_from_cache` spans are long, we hit KV cache contention and can increase cache shards. If `generate_tokens` is long -> model/kernel scheduling issue.
Alex M.: Nice runbook. One more: what metric exactly is TTFT? Is it `first_token_seconds` or `time_to_first_token_ms`?
Priya S.: The canonical metric is `first_token_seconds` (unit seconds). Grafana converts to ms in the panel. Prometheus label: `first_token_seconds{service="runtime-service", model=~".*"}`.
Marie L.: FYI, I'm going to open the PR to change the alert rule (infra/alerts#187) with the 10m eval + low-traffic guard. I'll cc @oncall if the change might affect paging. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Created issue infra/alerts#187: "Tweak runtime_latency_p99_high evaluation window + low-traffic guard". Link: https://git.redwood.internal/infra/alerts/issues/187
Alex M.: Thanks all. After the PR merges I'll re-run the query for the 03:20 window and post a small snippet of spans that show the candidate root cause. :eyes:
